papers.title: Periodic oscillatory slowing and aperiodic broadband shifts in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder are associated with phenoconversion.
papers.summary: In 134 patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder and 51 healthy controls, periodic and aperiodic EEG components were separated using FOOOF. Higher posterior periodic 4-8 Hz power and aperiodic offset were associated with phenoconversion to Parkinson's disease or dementia with Lewy bodies, and correlated with cognitive and motor measures.

papers.title: SPAR-EEG: Selective Pass-Wise Artifact Reduction for Wearable Single-Channel EEG Denoising.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: SPAR-EEG is a self-contained framework for single-channel EEG denoising that applies artifact-specific attenuation passes based on variational mode decomposition and singular spectrum analysis. It achieved the largest average artifact-region SNR improvements (9.05, 8.28, and 8.00 dB for EMG, EOG, and combined contamination, respectively) across 26 EEGdenoiseNet SNR levels compared to wavelet, EMD, and WQN baselines, and improved P300 speller accuracy by 7.8 percentage points.

papers.title: Improved detection and spatiotemporal spectral analysis of neural traveling waves
papers.summary: The paper introduces TWINDEX, a framework for three-dimensional spatiotemporal spectral analysis of neural traveling waves that generalizes to irregular sensor layouts and separates planar from standing waves. Applied to marmoset ECoG and human EEG, it identified alpha/low-beta traveling waves with physiologically plausible propagation speeds occurring in oppositely directed propagation modes across trials and epochs.

papers.title: iMINDBench: iEEG Multi-Institution Neural Decoding Benchmark
papers.summary: Presents iMINDBench, an iEEG benchmark of fifteen decoding tasks across three naturalistic movie-watching datasets with standardized preprocessing tracks and fixed evaluation splits. Evaluated pretrained systems generally outperformed baselines within their preprocessing tracks, but strong spectral baselines remained competitive, and adding up to 25x more supervised data from other subjects or institutions yielded only small or task-dependent gains.

papers.title: Honest and Reliable Evaluation and Expert Equivalence Testing of Automated Neonatal Seizure Detection.
papers.summary: Proposes evidence-based reporting recommendations for evaluating machine-learning neonatal EEG seizure detection under class imbalance and uncertain ground truth, based on tests with real and synthetic annotations. Matthews and Pearson's correlation coefficients outperformed AUC-ROC under class imbalance, and the multi-rater statistical Turing test using Fleiss' kappa was the most consistent human-expert equivalence test, leading to recommendations for balanced metrics, sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV, seizure-burden agreement, and multi-rater agreement on held-out validation sets.

papers.title: At-home limbic-targeted transcranial electrical stimulation during sleep: a feasibility study in healthy adults.
papers.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
papers.summary: Evaluated the feasibility of low-intensity, limbic-targeted transcranial electrical stimulation synchronized with N2 onset during sleep at home in 17 healthy adults using a sham-controlled protocol with overnight EEG. Limbic-targeted TES was associated with longer total sleep time and longer absolute N3 and REM durations, with REM also increased as a proportion of total sleep time, while the device was well tolerated and blinding maintained.

papers.title: Stacked EEG Spectrograms and an Attention-Augmented CNN-LSTM for Subject-Independent Emotion Recognition.
papers.summary: Proposes a stacked spectrogram representation that vertically concatenates channel-wise EEG spectrograms to preserve temporal, spectral, and channel information at the input level, combined with an attention-augmented CNN-LSTM for subject-independent emotion recognition. Under LOSO cross-validation the framework achieved 82.34% accuracy and 0.83 macro-F1 in four-class classification and 84.51% accuracy and 0.86 macro-F1 on SEED-IV, outperforming single-channel CNNs, stacked VGG16, and CNN-LSTM baselines with lower computational complexity.

papers.title: Entropy of the resting state cortex in epilepsy.
papers.summary: Analyzed resting-state MEG in 32 postsurgical epilepsy patients and week-long EEG in an LGI1-mAb rodent model to test whether interictal cortical entropy relates to seizure history. Lower age of seizure onset was associated with lower mean whole-cortex sample entropy; entropy did not differ between resected and non-resected regions, and LGI1-mAb rodents showed lower entropy after seizure onset than controls.

papers.title: Quantifying nociceptive state across the neuraxis with in vivo fiber photometry: methodological foundations, constraints, and future directions.
papers.summary: Reviews methodological foundations and constraints of in vivo fiber photometry for quantifying nociceptive state dynamics across the brain and spinal cord in rodents, emphasizing signal interpretation, artifact sources such as motion and hemodynamics, reference-channel strategies, and reporting standards. Highlights ascending nociceptive targets (parabrachial nucleus, periaqueductal gray, anterior cingulate cortex) and future directions including multisite/multicolor recordings and neuromodulator/voltage sensors.

papers.title: SWAS in SCN1A-related epilepsy: sleep EEG as a window into the evolving phenotype.
papers.journal: European journal of paediatric neurology : EJPN : official journal of the European Paediatric Neurology Society
papers.summary: Editorial commentary on sleep EEG as a window into the evolving phenotype of SCN1A-related epilepsy, specifically SWAS (sleep-related electrical status epilepticus/continuous spike-wave during sleep). No abstract is provided, so no specific findings can be summarized.

papers.title: Neural Reinstatement of Features in Audiovisual Working Memory Indicates Object-based Retrieval.
papers.summary: Using an EEG-based audiovisual delayed-match-to-sample task, this study tested whether attentional selection in working memory operates on unisensory features or bound cross-modal objects. Results showed that task-irrelevant features were retrieved in both auditory and visual probe trials, supporting object-based retrieval of bound audiovisual representations.

papers.title: Montage-guided fusion network for long-term scalp electroencephalography seizure detection.
papers.summary: The authors propose MGF-Net, a montage-guided fusion network that represents fixed bipolar EEG derivations as nodes in a relation-labeled graph and uses a relation-aware graph Transformer for seizure detection; on CHB-MIT it achieved 98.38% segment-level accuracy and detected all 65 test seizure events with 100% sensitivity, 0.82/h false detection rate, and 2.03 s latency.

papers.title: Advancing human sensorimotor research through modular robotics: the case of the HRX-1.
papers.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
papers.summary: This review/case study describes the HRX-1, a modular, portable, open-source single-degree-of-freedom robotic device for human sensorimotor research. It highlights applications in neuromechanics and rehabilitation, including integration with EMG, FES, and EEG for studies of dystonia, stroke, and functional neurological disorders.

papers.title: Towards a Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) for Improving Phonological Processing in Developmental Dyslexia: An Exploratory Study
papers.summary: Exploratory study testing an EEG-based brain-computer interface aimed at improving phonological processing in developmental dyslexia, using auditory input and visual feedback and targeting theta/delta dynamics from Temporal Sampling theory. In adults with and without dyslexia across 16 sessions, offline BCI learning scores were significantly associated with improvements in nonword reading, and also with real word reading and amplitude rise time discrimination.

papers.title: From signal to construct evidence: multimodal consumer-wearable sensing in real general-aviation flight.
papers.summary: In 40 pilots flying standardized maneuvers in a Cessna 172, multimodal wearable signals were assessed in nested evidence tiers; cardiac and oculomotor channels showed the strongest within-person convergence, but criterion-related frontal theta/alpha associations did not survive resampling and sensor features did not exceed a maneuver-only baseline in held-out pilots.

papers.title: Epilepsy: Bridging Epidemiological Landscapes, Molecular Mechanisms, and Emerging Precision Therapeutics.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes epidemiological disparities, molecular mechanisms including ion channel dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and mTOR dysregulation, and emerging precision diagnostics and therapeutics for epilepsy. It emphasizes individualized precision medicine approaches integrating genomics, biomarkers, and intelligent monitoring.

papers.title: Time-Varying Effective Network of Rehabilitation in Parkinson's Disease With Disease Laterality: A TMS-EEG Study.
papers.summary: In 27 left-affected and 27 right-affected Parkinson's disease patients undergoing 2-week multidisciplinary intensive rehabilitation therapy, single-pulse TMS-EEG with adaptive directed transfer function analysis revealed lateralized network changes, including decreased connectivity from the right central region to the parietal cortex in LPD patients correlating with axial symptom improvement and decreased whole-brain transfer efficiency in RPD patients correlating with motor improvement.

papers.title: Reactive Compensation for Proactive Deficits in Parkinsons Disease
papers.summary: In 30 Parkinson's disease patients and 30 healthy controls, a numerical Stroop task with EEG compared proactive and reactive cognitive control. PD patients showed reduced proactive control, absent N450, and compensatory LPC activity during proactive trials, suggesting reliance on reactive mechanisms to offset proactive deficits.

papers.title: Neural origins of the acoustic change complex auditory evoked potential: Topographical maps and source localization in the auditory cortex.
papers.summary: High-density 128-channel EEG in 18 normal-hearing adults with a 1 kHz pure tone and 10% frequency change was used to produce acoustic change complex topographical maps and source localization, showing P1-N1-P2 responses and bilateral N1 localization in auditory cortex similar to sound-onset generators.

papers.title: Intracranial recordings in humans reveal differential contributions of medial and lateral orbitofrontal cortex to approach-avoidance decision-making.
papers.summary: Intracranial stereotactic EEG recordings in humans performing a gamified approach-avoidance task identified pre-approach increases in medial orbitofrontal cortex activity and decreases in lateral orbitofrontal cortex activity, with rapid alternation between pro-approach and pro-avoidant states.

papers.title: Cross-device reproducibility of fNIRS biomarkers in SLE via EEG spatial mapping: a dual-site study.
papers.summary: A dual-site study of fNIRS during verbal fluency developed an EEG spatial prior mapping-based weighted common spatial pattern-support vector machine framework that achieved AUCs of 0.786 and 0.839 for classifying systemic lupus erythematosus versus controls and identified convergent right frontal and frontotemporal contributions, with CSP features negatively correlated with SLEDAI and HAMD.

papers.title: Dexmedetomidine induces bradycardia through vagal-nucleus tractus solitarius glutamatergic circuit.
papers.summary: In male mice, dexmedetomidine induced dose-dependent bradycardia while increasing phosphorylated ERK-positive glutamatergic neurons and firing in the vagal nodose ganglion, and chemogenetic inactivation of the vagal-nucleus tractus solitarius glutamatergic circuit reversed the bradycardia. The study identifies direct activation of vagal nodose ganglion neurons and vagal-NTS glutamatergic signaling as a mechanism of dexmedetomidine-induced bradycardia.

papers.title: Measuring motor intent for BCI control-A comparative analysis of signal quality of simultaneously recorded vECoG and scalp EEG.
papers.summary: This comparative study directly compared signal quality between vascular electrocorticography (vECoG) using a stent-electrode array and scalp EEG in one participant with ALS during attempted ankle movements. It found that vECoG generally showed significantly stronger motor modulation per channel in some frequency bands and conditions, with both modalities exhibiting significant modulation during attempted movement, and vECoG was less susceptible to ocular artifacts but more prone to cardiac artifacts.

papers.title: Longitudinal EEG, Seizure, and Developmental Patterns in Children With CDKL5 Deficiency Disorder in the First 2 Years of Life.
papers.summary: This multicenter longitudinal study analyzed 152 EEGs from 48 children with CDKL5 deficiency disorder during the first 2 years of life, finding that EEG background severity and interictal epileptiform burden worsened with age. Paroxysmal fast activity was more common in parieto-occipital regions, and its presence, along with hypsarrhythmia and epileptic encephalopathy, correlated with lower developmental scores; the highest discriminatory age for high-severity EEG was 9 months.

papers.title: Integrating Single-Molecule Variant Phenotyping with Clinical Features Predicts Outcomes in KIF1A-Associated Neurological Disorder
papers.summary: This study integrated single-molecule biophysical phenotyping of 91 pathogenic KIF1A variants with longitudinal clinical data from 343 patients with KIF1A-associated neurological disorder. A combined biophysical, computational pathogenicity, and clinical framework classified stable versus declining trajectories with AUC 0.834 and predicted VABS Adaptive Behavior Composite scores with R2 = 0.484 under leave-one-out cross-validation.

papers.title: N1 Suppression to Audiovisual Self-generated Sensory Events.
papers.summary: Two EEG studies examined N1 and P2 sensory attenuation for self-initiated audiovisual stimuli compared to unisensory stimuli. The results showed that multisensory audiovisual stimuli elicited N1 attenuation comparable to unisensory auditory stimuli, while no N1 attenuation was observed for unisensory visual stimuli, suggesting action-dependent mechanisms across modalities.

papers.title: Feasibility of multimodal behavioral, gaze, and EEG measurement of natural scene segmentation in autism
papers.summary: The authors present a multimodal experimental framework combining trial-based perceptual reports, EEG, and eye-tracking to study natural scene segmentation in autism. In a pilot study, neurotypical participants and participants with ASD aged 16 and older successfully performed the task and produced interpretable subjective segmentation maps, enabling analysis of reaction time distributions, gaze profiles, and trial-aligned neural responses.

papers.title: Systemic inflammatory profiles associated with early EEG abnormalities following ischemic stroke: a cohort study.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 307 acute supratentorial ischemic stroke patients with EEG within 72 h, elevated neutrophil count was independently associated with early epileptiform discharges (OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.05–1.36) and improved model discrimination, while no inflammatory biomarker independently predicted slow-wave activity after adjustment.

papers.title: Neurofeedback for functional neurological disorders: future directions for research and clinical practice.
papers.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
papers.summary: This opinion article synthesizes current neuroscientific models of functional neurological disorder (FND) with evidence from neurofeedback research in motor, affective, and pain-related conditions to explore neurofeedback as a potential intervention. It discusses modality-target considerations, learning mechanisms, and methodological variability, and outlines steps toward standardization while noting that empirical evidence remains preliminary.

papers.title: Multimodal integration supports neural processing of grammatical negation.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: Using EEG in Turkish, a verb-final language, this study investigated the neurocognition of multimodal negation and the contribution of gestures and prosodic markers. It found that gestures elicited an N100 effect and reduced the N400 amplitude in anticipation of the postverbal negation suffix, with prosody strengthening this N400 reduction only when gestures were present, providing evidence that multimodal information supports core grammatical operations.

papers.title: Animate-Inanimate Object Categorization from Minimal Visual Information in the Human Brain, Human Behavior, and Deep Neural Networks.
papers.summary: Using frequency-tagging EEG in healthy adults and deep neural networks, the study shows that the animate-inanimate distinction is preserved even for unrecognizable images retaining only low- or mid-level visual features. Significant neural responses at 1.2 Hz indicated rapid and automatic categorization, with similar effects in DNNs, demonstrating that animacy emerges early in the visual hierarchy and is resilient to visual information loss.

papers.title: Connectivity- and frequency-individualized accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation in treatment-resistant depression: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This randomized, placebo-controlled trial tested connectivity- and frequency-individualized accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (aiTBS) against sham stimulation in 51 patients with treatment-resistant depression. No significant differences were observed between active and sham arms on primary or secondary depression severity endpoints, indicating that personalized aiTBS failed to yield significant antidepressant benefits over sham.

papers.title: Transient Postoperative Myoclonus Following Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest.
papers.summary: A 72-year-old man developed transient bilateral myoclonus, diffuse rigidity, and suspected eyelid apraxia after ascending aorta and hemiarch replacement under hypothermic circulatory arrest; symptoms resolved by postoperative day 3 with levetiracetam and calcium supplementation, and he was discharged neurologically intact.

papers.title: Fahr syndrome in an 18-year-old male with pseudohypoparathyroidism: Clinical-radiological dissociation.
papers.summary: An 18-year-old male with pseudohypoparathyroidism and medication non-compliance presented with headaches, carpopedal spasms, and depressed mood, with extensive bilateral intracranial calcifications on CT/MRI but largely unremarkable neurological examination; calcium and calcitriol optimization resolved spasms and improved symptoms at 15 days.

papers.title: Enablers of Sustainable Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery: A Qualitative Exploration of Global Neurosurgery.
papers.summary: This qualitative study interviewed nine interdisciplinary providers involved in a Uganda–US pediatric epilepsy surgery collaboration and identified four themes for sustainable global neurosurgery program development: intentional planning, interdisciplinary collaboration, skill transfer and education, and targets for future work. The authors conclude that sustainable programs require trust, open communication, intentional planning, humility, and bidirectional skill transfer.

papers.title: Decoding co-encapsulation of β-carotene and tocopherol in zein nanoparticles through orthogonal spectroscopy and machine learning.
papers.summary: Zein nanoparticles co-loaded with tocopherol and β-carotene at different ratios were characterized using FTIR, fluorescence, and Raman hyperspectral imaging with machine learning. Tocopherol enhanced β-carotene encapsulation efficiency and antioxidant activity, with a 1:2 βC:TC ratio showing favorable intermolecular interactions and a 1:3 ratio suggesting perturbed non-covalent interactions; TC also helped preserve βC thermal stability.

papers.title: A protocol for potentially averting takotsubo syndrome following electrophysiology procedures.
papers.journal: Journal of interventional cardiac electrophysiology : an international journal of arrhythmias and pacing
papers.summary: This letter/comment proposes a protocol for potentially averting takotsubo syndrome following electrophysiology procedures. No abstract was supplied, so no specific results can be reported.

papers.title: Long-term outcomes following electrophysiology study for ventricular arrhythmia evaluation in congenital heart disease: A retrospective cohort study.
papers.journal: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
papers.summary: In 174 patients with congenital heart disease who underwent electrophysiology study with programmed ventricular stimulation for ventricular arrhythmia evaluation, inducibility identified a distinct phenotype but was not associated with worse long-term mortality/transplantation or ventricular arrhythmia outcomes over a median 13-year follow-up. A negative EPS did not exclude clinically relevant arrhythmic risk, as 20.4% of non-inducible patients later received an ICD.

papers.title: Intrathecal IgG synthesis as a biomarker for CNS involvement in anti-GQ1b antibody syndrome: a case report and hypothesis-generating treatment framework.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 37-year-old woman with a relapsing GBS–Miller Fisher syndrome–Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis overlap phenotype who showed cerebrospinal fluid evidence of intrathecal IgG synthesis (IgG index 1.13, synthesis rate 147.10 mg/24h, oligoclonal bands type III) alongside albuminocytologic dissociation. The authors hypothesize that intrathecal IgG synthesis may complement albuminocytologic dissociation as a biomarker of CNS involvement in anti-GQ1b antibody syndromes and could inform treatment intensity, requiring prospective testing.

papers.title: Revealing the potential of Gastrodia elata as a therapeutic candidate for degenerative diseases.
papers.summary: Ethanolic extracts of Gastrodia elata rhizomes were phytochemically profiled and tested for antioxidant activity, with gastrodin confirmed as the major bioactive compound. The extract showed strong DPPH radical scavenging and molecular docking/pharmacokinetic analyses supported gastrodin as a safe, potential therapeutic for oxidative stress and neurodegenerative conditions.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
